title: PG-DyRA: Potential-Game Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration for Dynamic Urban Resource Allocation

problem.claim: Urban public-resource allocation requires coordinating multiple mobile units to serve heterogeneous demands under coupled physical constraints and limited local observability.

gap.claim: Effective coordination must reason about unobserved agent actions despite sensing, communication, and privacy constraints, while the proposed setting assumes no inter-agent communication.

contributions.claim: PG-DyRA is a decentralized coordination framework for multi-agent urban resource allocation under partial observability without inter-agent communication.
The framework uses a marginal-contribution utility based on a potential-game formulation in which pure-strategy Nash equilibria coincide with the global optimum.

A dual-branch intention-inference network estimates other agents' service-capacity allocation from local observations by modeling visible agents through trajectory-based state-bank alignment and invisible agents through demand residuals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four urban datasets reportedly show 2.23–8.04 percentage points higher task coverage rates than state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report 2.99–8.35 percentage points lower energy consumption than state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban public-resource allocation is important for operational efficiency and service equity.
The task involves coordinating mobile units under heterogeneous demand, physical constraints, and restricted information.
The paper proposes a decentralized framework operating under partial observability without inter-agent communication.
A potential-game utility provides a theoretically grounded signal whose pure-strategy equilibria coincide with the global optimum.
A dual-branch intention-inference network supports local coordination, and experiments report improved coverage and reduced energy consumption.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines a global coordination objective with local intention inference under partial observability.

interpretation.claim: A theoretically aligned utility can provide a coordination target when agents cannot directly communicate or observe the full system.

application.claim: Similar designs may be applicable to multi-agent allocation problems with coupled constraints and restricted information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the evaluated urban datasets or observability assumptions.

unknowns: The four urban datasets are not identified.
The state-of-the-art comparison methods and experimental settings are not specified.
The abstract does not provide ablations, statistical uncertainty, or implementation and reproducibility details.
